subject: Clarify hosted rate card: Chat Completions vs Responses vs legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@northbound.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northbound.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick: hosted rate card + units question

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Procurement and engineering at Northbound are reviewing Redwood for a chat-centric feature set. Before we lock in a POC, we need a couple of clarifications on how you bill hosted usage so finance can map to our chargeback model:

- We see multiple endpoint names in the docs (Chat Completions, Responses, "legacy" completion endpoints). Can you confirm whether these are billed differently or if they map to the same billing units?
- For budgeting, we need 2 example invoices: (a) a high-chat scenario (10M input tokens / 3M output tokens monthly) and (b) a short-response-heavy scenario (6M small requests, average 40 tokens output). Show how line items will appear.
- Any standard discount schedule for a 12-month 200k USD monthly committed spend?

Appreciate a concise mapping/table — procurement prefers something we can paste into an internal doc. If easier, we can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Product, Northbound Logistics
attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@northbound.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: hosted rate card + units question

Hi Alex — great to hear from you. Short answers first, then I attached a tidy rate card (redwood_ratecard_v2027_q4.pdf) and a sample usage CSV so our billing examples are explicit.

High-level mapping (please treat the sample numbers as illustrative; final invoice lines will reflect your actual usage mix):
- Legacy endpoints (text/completions): billed per token (input + output) under the legacy-completions SKU.
- Chat Completions (conversation API): billed per token as well, but under the chat-completions SKU — same token accounting (input + output) but separate SKU for visibility and routing.
- Responses (new unified endpoint): we bill Responses under the responses SKU where requests are measured as "response units" that combine call count and tokens (we surface both token and RU line items on invoices). For most customers: short single-turn requests can look like a per-call RU charge with a small token charge; long conversation workloads show mostly token charges.

What I'll send in the attached examples:
- Example invoice A (high-chat): splits by SKU (chat-completions tokens, KV-cache savings line, and a small responses fallbacks line for tools).
- Example invoice B (response-heavy): shows RU line items + token lines for outputs, and an estimated effective $/1k token metric so your finance team can compare apples-to-apples.

To make the tables exact I need one quick datapoint from your side: of the total monthly requests above, how many are multi-turn conversational sessions versus single-turn responses? If you can drop a rough percentage (we can use 70/30 if you don't have it), I'll regenerate the sample invoices.

If you prefer a walkthrough, I've got 10–11am PT and 3–4pm PT slots tomorrow.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_ratecard_v2027_q4.pdf, northbound_sample_usage.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@northbound.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: hosted rate card + units question

Alex — adding a little more color on the mapping so your engineers can model it directly: 

- Token accounting: both legacy completions and chat-completions are token-based (input+output). We'll supply token logs per API key (daily) so you can reconcile.
- Responses SKU specifics: Responses introduces a RU abstraction that makes short-turn, high QPS workloads more economical in practice. Invoice shows: RU count, RU price, token output price. Example: a 30-token reply might appear as 1 RU @ $0.001 + 30 tokens @ $0.0004/token (numbers illustrative).
- Fallbacks & routing: If you pin a model and we route to a cheaper quantized variant during burst, you'll see a separate line for model-variant discount (we call it "routing-adjustment" on invoices).

Attached is northbound_sample_usage.csv with two variants of your numbers plus a column with the invoice-line mapping we would generate. Also included a quick Discount SRO (sample rates) for commit tiers: 10% @ 50k/mo, 18% @ 100k/mo, 25% @ 200k/mo (12-month prepay or monthly commit + revenue agreement). These are starting points; legal/pricing will finalize.

If you'd like a worked example, I'll drop a sample invoice tomorrow morning if you confirm the chat/single-turn split.

-Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: northbound_sample_usage.csv
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@northbound.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: hosted rate card + units question

Thanks — that's helpful. For our POC footprint the split is roughly 65% multi-turn chat sessions and 35% single-turn responses.

Two quick asks from procurement:
1) If we commit to 12 months at $200k/mo, what is the best-possible discount you can commit to in writing (we're open to partial upfront).
2) Can you provide the sample invoice that maps to our numbers so our accounting team can sign off?

If you can get that to us by COB Thursday, we'll review and aim to have term feedback the following week.

Appreciate it,
Alex
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@northbound.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick: hosted rate card + units question

Alex — thanks for the split. We've generated a draft invoice and a short proposal (attached: proposal_northbound_sow_draft.docx and the CSV used to build the invoice). Highlights:

- Provisional commercial: 22% discount on list with a 12-month commit at $200k/month if you pick the quarterly invoicing option; 25% discount if you prepay 12 months upfront. These are draft commercial terms subject to final legal review.
- Invoice mapping: separate line items for chat-completions tokens, responses RUs, model-variant routing adjustments, and a single monthly commitment credit line. We've included an "effective $/1k token" row in the invoice to make comparison straightforward.
- Next steps: if that commercial framing works, we'll prepare a term sheet + DocuSign link and schedule a short (30m) pricing review with finance/legal.

I'm free tomorrow 10am PT to walk the invoice with your accounting team. I'll also upload the sample invoice to the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign preview link once legal clears the wording.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
